newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian banks to issue UES convertible bond.
newsitem.headline: Russian banks to issue UES convertible bond.

text.p: A consortium of banks plans to issue bonds convertible into shares in national power company Unified Energy System (UES), UES President Anatoly Dyakov said on Friday.
The banks acquired 8.5 percent of UES earlier this year, he told a news conference.
"The consortium will issue the corresponding securities on them (the 8.5 percent) -- convertible bonds," said Dyakov.
The consortium of 35 banks and companies, headed by Natsionalny Reservny Bank, bought the 8.5 percent packet from the government earlier this year at a special auction.
Dyakov said some of the bonds would be offered to foreign investors and be similar to Eurobonds but that the main aim was to attract domestic Russian funds.
"This will allow us to attract about one trillion roubles and invest it in construction of (power) stations," Dyakov said.

Dyakov did not say how UES would receive the money under the programme, and company officials, who did not want to be named, said details of the programme were still being worked out with the consortium.
Dyakov said the banks would seek to issue the securities on both the Russian and foreign securities market.

He said work on issuing American Depositary Receipts -- which allow shares to be traded on the U.S. market -- was continuing but on a reduced scale due to the government's sale of the 8.5 percent stake to the bank consortium.
The State Duma lower house of parliament on Friday passed a law limiting non-resident holdings in UES to 25 percent.
The law, which President Boris Yeltsin has already vetoed, will now proceed to the upper house, the Federation Council.
But Dyakov said the company would not restrict access of non-residents to UES shares.
"Freedom existed before and it will remain," Dyakov said.
The government currently owns 52.7 percent of UES while foreign investors own 27.8 percent.
Under the law passed on Friday, the state would retain 51 percent of the company after December 31, 1998 while about one percent would be put up for auction this year.
Private shareholders own the remaining 19.5 percent of the company.
The government has said it may tighten control over UES, one of a series of monopolies which it intends to restructure.
